thesis: Broadcom is the custom-silicon toll road of the AI build-out: Q2 FY2026 revenue $22.19B with record operating profit and free cash flow, Q3 guided to $29.4B on AI semiconductor revenue of $16B (+200% y/y), FY2026 AI revenue guided to $56B (+180%) and 2027 reiterated above $100B. The Apple partnership extension through 2031 (this week's +5.3% pop) removes the biggest single-customer risk. Offsets: Q2 slightly missed consensus, the Q3 AI guide underwhelmed some analysts (Erste downgrade July 7), and at ~$1.78T / 62x trailing the multiple already banks years of AI growth.
catalysts: Q3 FY2026 results (~September 2026): guidance $29.4B revenue with $16B AI semiconductor revenue (+200% y/y)
2027 AI revenue target above $100B - reiterated; any confirmation via new XPU customer wins re-rates
Apple partnership extended through 2031 (announced early July 2026)
Custom AI processor customer base expanding beyond Google/Meta/Apple hyperscaler set
VMware software segment margin expansion and dividend growth (capital-return support)
risk_factors: Hyperscaler capex dependence: Q2 miss plus a lighter-than-hoped Q3 AI guide already raised scale-back doubts (Erste downgrade to Hold, July 7, 2026)
Custom ASIC concentration: a handful of hyperscaler design wins drive the entire AI franchise; program cancellations are lumpy and opaque
62x trailing earnings leaves limited multiple room if 2027's $100B+ AI target slips
Debt-heavy balance sheet from the VMware acquisition constrains flexibility in a downturn
NVIDIA competitive response (NVLink openness, pricing) could compress custom-silicon economics

q2_fy2026_revenue.note: record operating profit and FCF (figures not itemized in coverage); slight miss vs 22.27B consensus
q2_fy2026_revenue.source: Broadcom Q2 FY2026 press release (investors.broadcom.com) / CNBC 2026-06-03
